## Introduction

The aim of this analysis is to compare the transfer sizes and volumes of three Ethereum stablecoins: USDC, USDT and DAI.

We retrieve up to 1,000 recent ERC-20 transfer events for each token and remove transfers with a value of zero.

```{r load-packages}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(httr2)
library(knitr)
```

## Data preparation

```{r api-key}
api_key <- Sys.getenv("ETHERSCAN_API_KEY")
```

We use the Etherscan `tokentx` endpoint to retrieve the transfers of each token.

```{r download-data}
get_transfers <- function(token, contract) {
  response <- request("https://api.etherscan.io/v2/api") |>
    req_url_query(
      chainid = 1,
      module = "account",
      action = "tokentx",
      contractaddress = contract,
      page = 1,
      offset = 1000,
      sort = "desc",
      apikey = api_key
    ) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)

  response$result |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    transmute(
      Token = token,
      Time = as.POSIXct(as.numeric(timeStamp), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
      Hash = hash,
      From = from,
      To = to,
      Amount = as.numeric(value) / 10^as.numeric(tokenDecimal)
    )
}

usdc <- get_transfers("USDC", "0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48")
usdt <- get_transfers("USDT", "0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7")
dai <- get_transfers("DAI", "0x6b175474e89094c44da98b954eedeac495271d0f")

stablecoins <- bind_rows(usdc, usdt, dai) |>
  filter(Amount > 0)

glimpse(stablecoins)
```

After removing zero-value transfers, the dataset contains `r scales::comma(nrow(stablecoins))` transfers: `r paste(paste(count(stablecoins, Token)$Token, scales::comma(count(stablecoins, Token)$n)), collapse = ", ")`.

# Challenge 1: How do transfer sizes differ?

CHALLENGE: "How do the transfer sizes of USDC, USDT and DAI differ?"

We summarize the transfer amounts of each stablecoin.

```{r transfer-size-summary}
transfer_sizes <- stablecoins |>
  group_by(Token) |>
  summarise(
    Transfers = n(),
    Minimum = min(Amount),
    Median = median(Amount),
    Mean = mean(Amount),
    Maximum = max(Amount)
  )

transfer_sizes |>
  mutate(across(Minimum:Maximum, ~ format(round(.x, 2), big.mark = ","))) |>
  kable()
```

`r transfer_sizes$Token[which.max(transfer_sizes$Median)]` has the highest median at `r scales::comma(max(transfer_sizes$Median), accuracy = 0.01)`. `r transfer_sizes$Token[which.max(transfer_sizes$Mean)]` has the highest mean at `r scales::comma(max(transfer_sizes$Mean), accuracy = 0.01)`. The mean exceeds the median for `r sum(transfer_sizes$Mean > transfer_sizes$Median)` of the `r nrow(transfer_sizes)` tokens, showing the effect of large transfers.

We compare the distributions on a logarithmic scale because the transfer amounts vary greatly.

```{r transfer-size-plot}
ggplot(data = stablecoins, mapping = aes(x = Token, y = Amount, fill = Token)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  labs(
    title = "Stablecoin transfer sizes",
    x = "Stablecoin",
    y = "Transfer amount (log scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The highest observed transfer belongs to `r transfer_sizes$Token[which.max(transfer_sizes$Maximum)]` and is worth `r scales::comma(max(transfer_sizes$Maximum), accuracy = 0.01)`. The smallest median is `r scales::comma(min(transfer_sizes$Median), accuracy = 0.01)` for `r transfer_sizes$Token[which.min(transfer_sizes$Median)]`.

We can also inspect the full distribution of transfer amounts.

```{r transfer-size-distribution, fig.height=8}
ggplot(data = stablecoins, mapping = aes(x = Amount, fill = Token)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, colour = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(
    data = transfer_sizes,
    mapping = aes(xintercept = Median, linetype = "Median"),
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = transfer_sizes,
    mapping = aes(xintercept = Mean, linetype = "Mean"),
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = 10^seq(-6, 8, 2),
    labels = scales::label_log()
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("Median" = "dashed", "Mean" = "dotted"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Token, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of stablecoin transfer sizes",
    x = "Transfer amount (log scale)",
    y = "Number of transfers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

For `r sum(transfer_sizes$Mean > transfer_sizes$Median)` of the `r nrow(transfer_sizes)` tokens, the mean is above the median. This indicates that a limited number of large transfers raise the average.

# Challenge 2: How much transfer volume does each stablecoin generate?

CHALLENGE: "How much transfer volume does each stablecoin generate?"

We calculate the total and average volume of the positive transfers retrieved for each stablecoin.

```{r transfer-volume}
transfer_volumes <- stablecoins |>
  group_by(Token) |>
  summarise(
    Transfers = n(),
    TotalVolume = sum(Amount),
    AverageVolume = mean(Amount)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(TotalVolume))

transfer_volumes |>
  mutate(across(c(TotalVolume, AverageVolume), ~ format(round(.x, 2), big.mark = ","))) |>
  kable()
```

`r transfer_volumes$Token[1]` has the highest total volume at `r scales::comma(transfer_volumes$TotalVolume[1], accuracy = 0.01)`, followed by `r transfer_volumes$Token[2]` at `r scales::comma(transfer_volumes$TotalVolume[2], accuracy = 0.01)` and `r transfer_volumes$Token[3]` at `r scales::comma(transfer_volumes$TotalVolume[3], accuracy = 0.01)`.

```{r transfer-volume-plot}
ggplot(
  data = transfer_volumes,
  mapping = aes(x = reorder(Token, TotalVolume), y = TotalVolume, fill = Token)
) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    mapping = aes(label = scales::comma(TotalVolume, accuracy = 1)),
    hjust = -0.1
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Transfer volume by stablecoin",
    x = "Stablecoin",
    y = "Total volume"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The volume of `r transfer_volumes$Token[1]` is `r round(transfer_volumes$TotalVolume[1] / transfer_volumes$TotalVolume[2], 1)` times that of `r transfer_volumes$Token[2]`. The average transfer values range from `r scales::comma(min(transfer_volumes$AverageVolume), accuracy = 0.01)` to `r scales::comma(max(transfer_volumes$AverageVolume), accuracy = 0.01)`.
